_comment: ONE GRAMMAR, TWO LANGUAGES, ONE TRUTH (faced#625).
The Apple integrations are TypeScript and the mail/messaging proxies are Python, so this grammar
will exist twice. Two implementations drift, and drift here is SILENT: a query means one thing in
mail and another in messages, and nobody finds out until somebody's search comes back empty.
Both implementations parse every case below and must agree. A dialect that drifts fails a test
Terms and phrases are folded: lowercased, accents stripped.

cases.why: bare words are optional terms, and they RANK rather than filter
quotes are the exact-match escape hatch
a leading minus excludes a word
a minus before a quoted run excludes the whole phrase, not a stray quote
accents fold, so a French message is found without typing the accent
single quotes work like double, because people type both
an empty query asks for nothing, and must never mean everything
a bare minus is a word, not an exclusion of nothing
extra whitespace is not a term
an unclosed quote does not swallow the rest of the query
